input: Fix the cracked grout in the entryway tiles

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether this is a few isolated cracks or widespread grout failure across the whole entryway changes the effort, materials, and approach entirely.
The type of grout currently in place (sanded, unsanded, epoxy) and tile material determines which repair product is compatible and how to apply it.
A strict budget determines whether this is a DIY fix with a $10 grout pen or a professional re-grouting job costing hundreds of dollars.
Knowing whether the user is doing this themselves or hiring a professional shapes every step of the plan, from tool sourcing to scheduling.
The entryway is high-traffic, so the curing time and the need to keep it passable affects when the work can be done and in what phases.
Grout color matching is critical — whether the user wants to match existing grout exactly or is open to a full color change affects product selection.
The user may consider it done when it simply looks clean again, or they may want a long-lasting waterproof seal — this sets the bar for what repair method is acceptable.

gold.taskTitle: Fix cracked grout in entryway tiles
gold.taskDescription: Repair the cracked grout lines in the entryway tile floor to restore appearance and prevent further damage.

questions.title: How much of the grout is cracked or damaged?
questions.description: Is this a few isolated crack lines, or is grout failing across most of the entryway? This determines the scale of the repair.

questions.title: What type of grout and tile are currently installed?
questions.description: Knowing whether the existing grout is sanded, unsanded, or epoxy — and the tile material — determines which repair products are compatible.

questions.title: Are you planning to do this yourself or hire someone?
questions.description: DIY vs. professional execution changes every step of the plan, from tool sourcing to scheduling and skill requirements.

questions.title: What is your budget for this repair?
questions.description: Budget sets the ceiling on approach — a few dollars for a grout pen, moderate spend for DIY re-grouting supplies, or a professional service call.

questions.title: When does the entryway need to be usable again?
questions.description: Grout repairs require curing time with no foot traffic. Knowing the deadline or daily usage pattern determines how to phase the work.

questions.title: Do you need the new grout to match the existing color exactly?
questions.description: Color matching affects which product to buy and whether a full re-grout of visible lines is needed to keep things looking uniform.

questions.title: What does a successful repair look like to you?
questions.description: Is the goal simply a clean, filled appearance, or does the repair need to be fully waterproof and long-lasting against heavy foot traffic?
